# Container With Most Water：為什麼可以捨棄較短的牆

兩面高牆若靠得太近，組成的容器容量也可能很小。在 LeetCode 11，必須一起考慮一對牆的高度與距離。

## 把圖像轉成數字

輸入 `height` 依序列出位置 `0, 1, ..., n - 1` 上各面垂直牆的高度。選擇兩個不同的位置 `i < j`，讓地面與兩面牆形成直立容器。回傳最大的容量，結果是一個 integer，而不是牆的位置。題目限制為 `2 <= n <= 100000`、`0 <= height[i] <= 10000`。題目沒有要求修改輸入，以下解法也都保留原始輸入。空輸入與只有一面牆的輸入不在這份 contract 內。[LeetCode 題目敘述](https://leetcode.com/problems/container-with-most-water/)。

水位不能高於較短的牆，否則水會從那一側流出去。水平距離是 `j - i`，算的是間隔數，而不是牆的數量。因此，一對牆的容量就是長方形截面面積：

`area(i, j) = (j - i) * min(height[i], height[j])`。

以自製範例 `[2, 5, 1, 4]` 而言，位置 `1` 與 `3` 的牆寬度為 `2`、水高為 `4`，面積是 `8`。位置 `0` 與 `3` 雖然更遠，面積卻只有 `3 * 2 = 6`。最高的牆本身無法決定答案。中間的牆不會讓這個長方形扣除相應高度；這個問題選擇的是兩個邊界，並不是把各處積存的雨水加起來。

若兩個選定高度都是零，面積也是零。所有高度都是零時，正確最大值就是零。因此，每個合法輸入都可以從 `best = 0` 開始。

## 先保留所有可能的配對

直接的解法是固定左邊位置，再嘗試它右邊的每個位置。`best` 保留目前算過的最大面積；保存舊配對的所有面積，只會增加儲存量，無助於下一次比較。

```python
def max_area_all_pairs(height: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(height)
    best = 0
    for i in range(n - 1):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            area = (j - i) * min(height[i], height[j])
            best = max(best, area)
    return best
```

`range(i + 1, n)` 產生從 `i + 1` 到 `n - 1` 的位置，不包含 `n`。因此每次取值都在合法範圍內，每對牆都不相同，也不會反過來重算同一對。`min(a, b)` 回傳較小的 argument；`max(best, area)` 回傳較大的值。兩者都不修改 list。這裡使用的是文件中 [Python built-in functions](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/functions.html) 的雙 argument 形式。

對 `[2, 5, 1, 4]`，六組配對依執行順序的面積為 `2, 2, 6, 1, 8, 1`。對應的 `best` 依序是 `2, 2, 6, 6, 8, 8`。因為每個候選都看過，最後回傳 `8`。

輸入接近上限時，候選數量就很重要。位置 `0` 有 `n - 1` 個搭檔，位置 `1` 有 `n - 2` 個，最後一個有用的左邊位置有 `1` 個。把這些數量正序、倒序各寫一次後相加，每組對應數的和都是 `n`，共有 `n - 1` 組。這樣把候選算了兩次，所以配對總數是 `n * (n - 1) / 2`。當 `n = 100000`，就要計算 `4,999,950,000` 次面積。若要跳過候選又不漏掉最大值，需要一個理由。

## 先計算尚未排除範圍中最寬的配對，再移除一面牆

保留 `left` 與 `right` 兩個 index，起初分別位於兩端。這裡稱它們為 two pointers；它們只是一般的整數位置，不是複製出來的 sublist，也不是 Python 記憶體位址。包含兩端的 `[left, right]` 區間，代表尚未解決配對可用的位置。捨棄任何位置前，先計算兩端形成的配對。

假設 `height[left] <= height[right]`。剛量到的面積是 `(right - left) * height[left]`。考慮保留 `left`，把 `right` 換成內部位置 `k` 的任何配對。新寬度 `k - left` 比原來小，而且即使新牆高很多，水高也不可能超過 `height[left]`。由於牆高非負，

`area(left, k) <= (k - left) * height[left] <= (right - left) * height[left]`。

所以這些配對都不可能勝過已記錄的兩端面積。把 `left` 加一，就能一次捨棄所有仍涉及 `left` 的候選。這是對它所有可能搭檔的上界證明，並不是預測下一面牆更高，也不是說下一次面積一定更大。

右牆較短時，把左右反過來即可：保留 `right`、把左邊往內移，不可能改善剛量過的面積，所以將 `right` 減一。若兩側一樣高，同一個不等式允許捨棄任一側。程式選擇捨棄左側。兩側同為零也安全，因為保留其中任何零高牆的配對，面積都是零。

這項規則會主動放棄寬度，但只有先證明失去的配對已被記錄值涵蓋，才移除牆。每次都移動較高牆的規則沒有這個證明。對 `[1, 3, 3]`，外側配對面積為 `2`。若把較高的右牆往內移，接著得到面積 `1`，最後回傳 `2`，卻漏掉位置 `1` 與 `2` 的面積 `3`。以牆的數量衡量，這是最小 counterexample：只有兩面牆時，在任何移動前就已算過唯一候選。

## 追蹤狀態直到回傳

對 `[2, 5, 1, 4]`，初始狀態是 `(left, right, best) = (0, 3, 0)`。

讀取 `height[0] = 2` 與 `height[3] = 4`。寬度為 `3`、水高為 `2`，面積是 `6`。先把 `best` 改成 `6`，再移動。因為 `2 <= 4`，將 `left` 加一，新狀態為 `(1, 3, 6)`。被跳過、仍保留位置 `0` 的配對，不可能超過剛量到的 `6`。

現在讀到高度 `5` 與 `4`。寬度為 `2`，面積是 `8`。`best` 變成 `8`。左牆較高，所以將 `right` 減一，得到 `(1, 2, 8)`。其中，配對 `(2, 3)` 可以安全捨棄：寬度是 `1`，水高不可能超過被捨棄右牆的高度 `4`。

讀到高度 `5` 與 `1`。寬度為 `1`，面積是 `1`。比較後 `best` 維持 `8`。再次將 `right` 減一，得到 `(1, 1, 8)`。此時 `left < right` 為 false：一個位置無法提供兩面不同的牆。回傳 `8`。

另外用 `[3, 3, 3]` 查看等高情況：先得到面積 `6`，移動左側，再量到面積 `3`，再次移動左側，最後回傳 `6`。移動後的當前面積可能變小；保存最大值才能保住先前答案。

```python
class Solution:
    def maxArea(self, height: list[int]) -> int:
        left = 0
        right = len(height) - 1
        best = 0

        while left < right:
            left_height = height[left]
            right_height = height[right]
            area = (right - left) * min(left_height, right_height)
            best = max(best, area)

            if left_height <= right_height:
                left += 1
            else:
                right -= 1

        return best
```

`while` 在每次執行迴圈主體前測試條件；`if` 恰好選擇一個 branch。因此，每次 iteration 恰好改動一個 index。[Python compound statements](https://docs.python.org/3.14/reference/compound_stmts.html)。

讀取 `height[left]` 會取出元素，但不會移除它。把值指派給 `left_height`，會綁定一個 local name，並不會複製 list。Python integer 是 immutable：`left += 1` 計算新的整數值，再將 `left` 綁定到它，不會改動 `height` 裡儲存的整數。若 assignment 的目標是 `height[left]` 這樣的 item，便會寫入該 item；這裡沒有這種 assignment。呼叫者仍能使用原始輸入。[Python assignments](https://docs.python.org/3.14/reference/simple_stmts.html#assignment-statements)、[numeric types](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/stdtypes.html#numeric-types-int-float-complex)。

## 每個檢查點都成立的事

面積公式描述的是單一配對。整個搜尋是否正確，還需要另一個 loop invariant：在指定檢查點持續成立的敘述。每次開始檢查 `while` 條件時，`best` 是所有已計算配對的最大面積；若尚未計算任何配對，它就是零。而任何一端位於當前區間之外的配對，面積都不超過 `best`。

起初 `[0, n - 1]` 外沒有任何位置，所以第二項敘述沒有被排除配對需要檢查。第一項也成立，因為 `best` 是零，而且所有合法面積都非負。

每次 iteration 量出兩端面積並更新 `best`，會保住第一項敘述。捨棄用的不等式證明，所有新排除配對的面積，都不超過剛量到的面積，也就不超過更新後的 `best`。由於 `best` 永不減少，先前排除的配對仍然被涵蓋。無論選哪個 branch，包括等高情況，這些事實都會重新建立 invariant。

距離 `right - left` 從 `n - 1` 開始，每次恰好減一。經過 `n - 1` 次 iteration，距離就變成零。此時，已沒有任何配對的兩端都能留在區間內，因此每個合法配對都已計算過，或被 invariant 涵蓋。除了不影響結果的初始零，`best` 也確實來自實際候選，因此它等於要求的最大值。

## 計算操作與儲存的值

令 `n` 表示牆的數量。我們用 bounded-integer、unit-cost model 比較成長：一次整數比較、加法、減法、乘法、local binding 或 indexed list access，都花費有界的工作量；儲存一個這樣的 scalar 或 reference 算一個單位。依題目限制，index 小於 `100000`，牆高至多 `10000`，面積至多為 `99999 * 10000 = 999,990,000`。這些值都能用固定數量、機器大小的整數片段表示。這個 model 計算工作量，並不是說所有 Python expression 的實際耗時相同。Python 能表示更大的整數，但若數字位數可以無限增加，就必須改用另一種 arithmetic cost model。

list access 的假設有具體的實作依據。在 CPython v3.14.0，list 將 element reference 存在以 index 定位的 slot；取得 slot `i` 會存取該 slot，而不是逐一走過前面 `i` 個元素。list 也儲存長度，因此 `len(height)` 不必逐面牆計數。在普通 list、沒有 concurrent mutation 的情況下，這些特性支持這種存取模式的有界工作量。[CPython list 實作](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Objects/listobject.c)、[list 結構與存取 macros](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Include/cpython/listobject.h)。

每次 two-pointer iteration 讀取 list 兩次、執行固定數量的有界算術與比較，並更新一個 index。`min` 與 `max` 各接收兩個 scalar，所以比較工作不會隨 `n` 增加。iteration 恰有 `n - 1` 次，迴圈條件檢查有 `n` 次；初始化與回傳增加固定工作。因此，總工作量可以被「某個常數乘以 `n`，再加上一個常數」限制。我們把這寫成 `O(n)` time。Big O 表示忽略固定乘數後的成長上界；這裡，精確的 iteration 次數也表明是線性成長，不只有上界。

同一時間，只有固定數量的 local name 與暫時 integer result 存活。後續 iteration 取代先前的值，不保存歷史。沒有 recursion、持續長大的 collection，也沒有複製輸入。Auxiliary space 指的是供應的輸入與回傳結果以外新增的儲存量，這裡為 `O(1)`。暫時算術值在同一時間也只占固定數量的有界單位。回傳單一 integer 的 output space 是 `O(1)`；呼叫者原本的 list 已占 `O(n)` 個單位，不計入 auxiliary space。

all-pairs 解法每個候選也使用相同的有界讀取、算術與雙 argument 比較。因此，`n * (n - 1) / 2` 次計算帶來 `O(n²)` time：隨著 `n` 增大，平方項主導成長。它仍然只需要 `O(1)` auxiliary space 與 `O(1)` output space。Python `range` 保留 start、stop、step，而不會把所有 index 都實體化。外層迴圈保留一個 range 與當前位置；每個內層 range 都取代前一個，不會留下配對 list 或面積歷史。即使執行期間建立過很多內層 range，同時存活的數量仍然固定。`n - 1` 次內層 range 初始化只儲存這些固定欄位，每次前進則遞增一個有界 integer index。在前述 elementary model 下，這些初始化增加線性工作量，每個候選的前進增加固定工作量；兩者都不超過平方級總量。[Python range objects](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/stdtypes.html#ranges)。

對很小的輸入，all-pairs 適合作為檢查用的 oracle：它直接列舉 contract 中的候選，所以容易核對。若新的計分規則破壞較短牆的上界，它也仍可作為起點；但改過的規則需要自己的成本分析與證明。在目前的 contract 與大輸入上限下，two-pointer 解法能避免數十億次計算，也不增加隨輸入成長的儲存量。

## 改變間距，保留理由

假設輸入還提供 strictly increasing 的整數座標 `x`，與 `height` 採相同順序，且 `0 <= x[i] <= 1000000000`。高度與長度限制維持原樣。牆之間不再一律相隔一單位。繼續用 `right - left`，算出的會是間隔數，而不是間隔的總寬度。

將寬度改為 `x[right] - x[left]`。對 `x = [0, 1, 100]` 與 `height = [1, 3, 2]`，外側配對的面積是 `100`；移動較短的左牆後，得到 `99 * 2 = 198`。答案是 `198`。原本用 index 算寬度則會回傳 `2`。

```python
def max_area_at_positions(x: list[int], height: list[int]) -> int:
    left = 0
    right = len(height) - 1
    best = 0
    while left < right:
        left_height = height[left]
        right_height = height[right]
        area = (x[right] - x[left]) * min(left_height, right_height)
        best = max(best, area)
        if left_height <= right_height:
            left += 1
        else:
            right -= 1
    return best
```

Strictly increasing 座標保證，任一端點往內移都會縮小實際寬度。較短牆對水高的上界沒有改變，所以把 index 差替換成座標差後，捨棄用的不等式與 invariant 仍成立。Pointer 每次仍只移動一個位置：座標間距的數值大小，不會增加 iteration 次數。

這項改版每次 iteration 多讀取兩個座標 slot；對座標值做減法，取代原本對 index 的減法。它沒有新增隨輸入成長的迴圈或 collection。座標與面積仍有界，面積至多 `1000000000 * 10000 = 10¹³`，在同一 model 下只需固定數量的 scalar 單位。因此，`n - 1` 次 iteration 仍帶來 `O(n)` time，固定的存活狀態則帶來 `O(1)` auxiliary 與 output space。新增的座標 list 是已提供的輸入，另外占 `O(n)` 單位，並不是函式自行配置的 list。這項推導假定座標已排序且與高度對應；函式不會排序，也不會驗證那個不同的 contract。

## Interview English 與 master map

Why move the shorter wall? Keeping it caps the water height while moving the other endpoint inward reduces width. All such pairs are bounded by the endpoint area already measured.

Does the next pair have to improve? No. `best` remembers earlier candidates, so the current area may decrease.

What happens on equal heights? Either endpoint can be removed safely. This implementation removes the left one.

Why is the time linear? The index distance decreases from `n - 1` to zero, once per constant-work iteration.

What does constant space exclude? It excludes the caller's input list. The function adds a fixed set of scalar locals and returns one integer.

Master map 是一串因果關係：兩個牆的位置決定寬度；較短牆決定水高；兩者相乘得到候選面積。已計算的候選，限制了所有保留較短牆、另一側往內移的配對。移除該牆，會縮小尚未解決的區間，同時由 `best` 涵蓋已排除配對。當區間無法包含兩面牆，`best` 就涵蓋每個合法選擇。

# Container With Most Water: why the shorter wall can be discarded

Two tall walls can make a poor container if they stand too close together. In LeetCode 11, the decision is about a pair's height and distance together.

## Turn the picture into a number

The input `height` lists vertical wall heights at positions `0, 1, ..., n - 1`. Choose two distinct positions `i < j`; the ground and those two walls form an upright container. Return the largest capacity, as an integer, rather than the wall positions. The statement allows `2 <= n <= 100000` and `0 <= height[i] <= 10000`. It does not ask us to change the input, and the solutions below leave it unchanged. Empty and one-wall inputs are outside this contract. [LeetCode problem statement](https://leetcode.com/problems/container-with-most-water/).

The water cannot rise above the shorter wall: it would spill over that side. The horizontal distance is `j - i`, counting gaps rather than walls. Thus a pair's capacity is its rectangular cross-sectional area:

`area(i, j) = (j - i) * min(height[i], height[j])`.

For the constructed input `[2, 5, 1, 4]`, walls at positions `1` and `3` give width `2`, water height `4`, and area `8`. Positions `0` and `3` are farther apart, but give only `3 * 2 = 6`. The tallest wall alone does not determine the answer. Intermediate walls do not subtract their height from this rectangle; this problem chooses two boundaries, rather than adding pockets of trapped rainwater.

If both chosen heights are zero, their area is zero. When all heights are zero, zero is the correct maximum. This makes `best = 0` a valid initial value for every legal input.

## First keep every possible pair

A direct solution fixes the left position and tries every position to its right. `best` retains the largest area evaluated so far; keeping the areas of old pairs would add storage without helping the next comparison.

```python
def max_area_all_pairs(height: list[int]) -> int:
    n = len(height)
    best = 0
    for i in range(n - 1):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            area = (j - i) * min(height[i], height[j])
            best = max(best, area)
    return best
```

`range(i + 1, n)` produces positions from `i + 1` through `n - 1`. It excludes `n`, so every lookup is valid, every pair has distinct walls, and a pair is not repeated in reverse. `min(a, b)` returns the smaller argument; `max(best, area)` returns the larger. Neither call changes the list. These are the two-argument forms of the documented [Python built-in functions](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/functions.html).

For `[2, 5, 1, 4]`, the six pairs in execution order have areas `2, 2, 6, 1, 8, 1`. The corresponding `best` values are `2, 2, 6, 6, 8, 8`; returning `8` therefore follows from examining every candidate.

The number of candidates matters at the upper input limit. To count them, position `0` has `n - 1` partners, position `1` has `n - 2`, and the last useful left position has `1`. Add these counts forward and backward: each matched sum is `n`, and there are `n - 1` such sums. That double-counts the candidates, giving `n * (n - 1) / 2` pairs. At `n = 100000`, that is `4,999,950,000` area evaluations. We need a reason to skip candidates without losing the maximum.

## Evaluate the widest remaining pair, then remove a wall

Keep two indices, `left` and `right`, initially at opposite ends. These indices are called two pointers here; they are ordinary integer positions, not copied sublists or Python memory addresses. The inclusive interval from `left` to `right` contains the positions still available for unresolved pairs. Evaluate its endpoint pair before discarding anything.

Suppose `height[left] <= height[right]`. The pair just measured has area `(right - left) * height[left]`. Consider any pair that keeps `left` and replaces `right` with an inner position `k`. Its width `k - left` is smaller, and its water height cannot exceed `height[left]`, even if the new wall is much taller. Because heights are nonnegative,

`area(left, k) <= (k - left) * height[left] <= (right - left) * height[left]`.

So no such pair can beat the endpoint area we already recorded. Every remaining candidate involving `left` can be discarded together by increasing `left` by one. This is a bound on all its possible partners, not a prediction that the next wall is taller or that the next area will improve.

When the right wall is shorter, the same argument applies with the sides reversed: keeping `right` while moving the left endpoint inward cannot improve the area just measured, so decrease `right`. If the heights are equal, either endpoint may be discarded by the same inequality. The code chooses to discard the left one. Zero-height ties remain safe because every pair keeping either zero-height wall has area zero.

This rule deliberately gives up width. It removes a wall only after proving that the lost pairs are already covered by a recorded value. Always moving the taller wall lacks that proof. On `[1, 3, 3]`, the outer pair gives area `2`. Moving the taller right wall inward then gives area `1`, and the process returns `2`; it misses positions `1` and `2`, whose area is `3`. This is a smallest counterexample by number of walls: with two walls, the only candidate is evaluated before any move.

## Follow the state all the way to the return

On `[2, 5, 1, 4]`, begin with `(left, right, best) = (0, 3, 0)`.

Read `height[0] = 2` and `height[3] = 4`. Width is `3`, water height is `2`, and area is `6`. Replace `best` with `6` before moving. Since `2 <= 4`, increase `left`: the new state is `(1, 3, 6)`. The skipped pairs keeping position `0` cannot exceed the measured `6`.

Now read heights `5` and `4`. Width is `2`, so area is `8`. `best` becomes `8`. The left wall is taller, so decrease `right`, giving `(1, 2, 8)`. In particular, pair `(2, 3)` is safely discarded: its width is `1`, and its height cannot exceed the discarded right wall's height `4`.

Read heights `5` and `1`. Width is `1`, giving area `1`. The comparison leaves `best` at `8`. Decrease `right` again, reaching `(1, 1, 8)`. The condition `left < right` is now false: one position cannot supply two distinct walls. Return `8`.

A separate tie witness, `[3, 3, 3]`, starts with area `6`, moves left, measures area `3`, moves left again and returns `6`. A move can reduce the current area; the saved maximum prevents losing the earlier answer.

```python
class Solution:
    def maxArea(self, height: list[int]) -> int:
        left = 0
        right = len(height) - 1
        best = 0

        while left < right:
            left_height = height[left]
            right_height = height[right]
            area = (right - left) * min(left_height, right_height)
            best = max(best, area)

            if left_height <= right_height:
                left += 1
            else:
                right -= 1

        return best
```

The `while` statement tests its condition before each execution of the body; `if` selects exactly one branch. Thus exactly one index changes per iteration. [Python compound statements](https://docs.python.org/3.14/reference/compound_stmts.html).

Reading `height[left]` retrieves an element without removing it. Assigning that value to `left_height` binds a local name; it does not copy the list. Python integers are immutable: `left += 1` computes an integer value and rebinds `left`, rather than changing an integer stored inside `height`. An assignment targeting an item such as `height[left]` would write that item; no such assignment occurs here. The input remains available to the caller. [Python assignments](https://docs.python.org/3.14/reference/simple_stmts.html#assignment-statements), [numeric types](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/stdtypes.html#numeric-types-int-float-complex).

## What stays true at every checkpoint

The area formula describes one pair. Correctness of the whole search needs a separate loop invariant, a statement that remains true at a chosen checkpoint. At the start of every `while` condition check: `best` is the maximum area among pairs already evaluated, or zero if none were evaluated; every pair with an endpoint outside the current interval has area at most `best`.

Initially there are no positions outside `[0, n - 1]`, so the second claim has no excluded pairs to check. The first claim holds because `best` is zero and all legal areas are nonnegative.

During an iteration, measuring the endpoints and updating `best` preserves the first claim. The discard inequality proves that every newly excluded pair has area at most the area just measured, which is at most the updated `best`. Previously excluded pairs remain covered because `best` never decreases. These facts reestablish the invariant for either branch, including equal heights.

The distance `right - left` starts at `n - 1` and decreases by exactly one each time. It reaches zero after `n - 1` iterations. At that point no pair has both endpoints in the remaining interval, so every legal pair has been evaluated or covered by the invariant. Since `best` also comes from actual candidates, except for the harmless initial zero, it equals the required maximum.

## Account for operations and stored values

Let `n` be the number of walls. We compare growth using a bounded-integer, unit-cost model: one integer comparison, addition, subtraction, multiplication, local binding, or indexed list access costs a bounded amount; storing one such scalar or reference uses one unit. For this statement, indices are below `100000`, heights are at most `10000`, and an area is at most `99999 * 10000 = 999,990,000`. These values fit within a fixed number of machine-sized integer pieces. This model counts work, not equal physical time for all Python expressions. Python can represent larger integers, but an unbounded increase in their digit count would require a different arithmetic cost model.

The list-access assumption has a concrete implementation basis. In CPython v3.14.0, a list stores element references in indexed slots; fetching slot `i` accesses that slot rather than walking through the preceding `i` elements. Its length is stored, so `len(height)` does not count the walls one by one. These properties support bounded work for this access pattern, with an ordinary list and no concurrent mutation. [CPython list implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Objects/listobject.c), [list structure and access macros](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Include/cpython/listobject.h).

Each two-pointer iteration makes two list reads, a fixed number of bounded arithmetic and comparison operations, and one index update. `min` and `max` each receive two scalar values, so their comparison work does not grow with `n`. There are exactly `n - 1` iterations and `n` loop-condition checks; setup and return add fixed work. Thus total work is bounded by a constant times `n` plus a constant. We write this as `O(n)` time. Big O expresses an upper growth bound, ignoring fixed multipliers; here the exact iteration count also gives linear growth, not just an upper limit.

Only a fixed number of local names and temporary integer results are live at once. Later iterations replace earlier values rather than retaining a history. There is no recursion, growing collection or copied input. Auxiliary space, meaning storage added beyond the supplied input and returned result, is `O(1)`. Transient arithmetic values also occupy only a fixed number of bounded units at once. The returned single integer is `O(1)` output space; the caller's original list already occupies `O(n)` units and is excluded from auxiliary space.

The all-pairs solution uses the same bounded reads, arithmetic and two-argument comparisons for each candidate. Its `n * (n - 1) / 2` evaluations therefore give `O(n²)` time: for growing `n`, the squared term dominates. Its space is still `O(1)` auxiliary and `O(1)` output. A Python `range` retains its start, stop and step rather than materializing all indices. The outer loop keeps one range and its current position; each inner range replaces the previous one, and no pair list or area history survives. Even though many inner ranges are created over time, only a fixed number are live simultaneously. The `n - 1` inner-range setups store only these fixed fields, and each step advances a bounded integer index. Under the stated elementary model, those setups add linear work and each step adds fixed work per candidate; neither exceeds the quadratic total. [Python range objects](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/stdtypes.html#ranges).

For tiny inputs, all-pairs is useful as a checking oracle: it is easy to inspect because it directly enumerates the contract's candidates. It also remains a starting point if a new scoring rule destroys the shorter-wall bound; that changed rule would need its own costs and proof. Under the present contract and large input limit, the two-pointer solution avoids billions of evaluations with no extra growing storage.

## Change the spacing, preserve the reason

Suppose the input supplies strictly increasing integer coordinates `x`, in the same order as `height`, with `0 <= x[i] <= 1000000000`. Keep the original height and length limits. Walls no longer stand one unit apart. Reusing `right - left` would calculate the number of gaps, rather than their total width.

Replace the width by `x[right] - x[left]`. On `x = [0, 1, 100]` and `height = [1, 3, 2]`, the outer pair has area `100`; moving the shorter left wall reveals area `99 * 2 = 198`. The answer is `198`. The original index-width calculation would instead return `2`.

```python
def max_area_at_positions(x: list[int], height: list[int]) -> int:
    left = 0
    right = len(height) - 1
    best = 0
    while left < right:
        left_height = height[left]
        right_height = height[right]
        area = (x[right] - x[left]) * min(left_height, right_height)
        best = max(best, area)
        if left_height <= right_height:
            left += 1
        else:
            right -= 1
    return best
```

Strictly increasing coordinates ensure that moving either endpoint inward decreases physical width. The shorter-wall height bound is unchanged, so the discard inequality and invariant still hold with coordinate differences replacing index differences. The pointers still move by one position per iteration: the numerical size of a coordinate gap does not add iterations.

The adaptation adds two coordinate-slot reads per iteration; subtracting their values replaces the old index subtraction. It adds no growing loop or collection. Coordinates and areas remain bounded, with area at most `1000000000 * 10000 = 10¹³`, fitting a fixed number of scalar units under the same model. Consequently the `n - 1` iterations still give `O(n)` time and fixed live state gives `O(1)` auxiliary and output space. The additional coordinate list is supplied input, using another `O(n)` units, rather than a list allocated by the function. This argument assumes coordinates arrive ordered and matched to heights; the function neither sorts nor verifies that different contract.

## Interview English and the master map

Why move the shorter wall? Keeping it caps the water height while moving the other endpoint inward reduces width. All such pairs are bounded by the endpoint area already measured.

Does the next pair have to improve? No. `best` remembers earlier candidates, so the current area may decrease.

What happens on equal heights? Either endpoint can be removed safely. This implementation removes the left one.

Why is the time linear? The index distance decreases from `n - 1` to zero, once per constant-work iteration.

What does constant space exclude? It excludes the caller's input list. The function adds a fixed set of scalar locals and returns one integer.

The master map is a chain of reasons: two wall positions determine width; the shorter wall determines water height; their product evaluates a candidate. An evaluated candidate bounds every inward pair retaining its shorter wall. Removing that wall shrinks the unresolved interval while `best` covers excluded pairs. When the interval cannot contain two walls, `best` covers every legal choice.

# Course Schedule：計算尚未滿足的先修義務

假設課程 3 同時要求先修完課程 1 與課程 2。完成課程 1 有幫助，但課程 3 仍不能開始。解法必須記住還有幾項要求，並察覺這個數量降到零的時刻。

## 完成所有課程代表什麼

在 [LeetCode 207](https://leetcode.com/problems/course-schedule/) 中，課程識別碼從 `0` 到 `numCourses - 1`。一組 `[a, b]` 表示必須先完成 `b`，才能修 `a`。回傳一個 Boolean，表示是否能完成每門課；不需要回傳 schedule 本身。課程數介於 1 到 2000，互不重複的 prerequisite pairs 數量介於 0 到 5000；兩個識別碼都在課程範圍內。題目沒有排除 `[a, a]`，而這會讓該課程無法開始。下面的實作不修改輸入。

沒有先修要求的課程可以立即修讀。即使某門課沒有出現在任何 pair 裡，它仍然存在，也必須計入結果。相反地，`[[1, 0], [0, 1]]` 讓課程 0 與課程 1 彼此等待。無論選哪門當第一門，都無法滿足這些要求。

對每組 `[a, b]` 畫一條 directed edge `b -> a`。一張 directed graph，就是所有課程節點以及這些單向的先修 edges。沿著一條或多條 edges 回到起點，就形成 directed cycle。cycle 上的每門課都必須等待同一個 cycle 裡的另一門課，因此不可能先完成其中任何一門。self-loop 是只含一個節點的 cycle。

對這張有限的 graph，反過來也成立。如果每門尚未完成的課，都還有一門尚未完成的 prerequisite，就從任一門未完成的課出發，不斷往回追它的 prerequisite。課程識別碼的數量有限，因此必定重遇某個識別碼，於是找到 cycle。所以，只要剩餘部分非空而且沒有 cycle，就必定有課程可以開始。不斷選一門可開始的課，能恰好在 graph 沒有 directed cycle 時完成所有課程。這個 equivalence 描述題目的性質；實作則會由隨執行狀態變化的 loop invariant 來描述。

## 保存計數，以及它可以釋放哪些課程

每完成一門課就掃描所有 pairs，會重新找出哪些課依賴剛完成的課。改為建立 `after[b]`，保存直接等待 `b` 的課程清單。對每組 `[a, b]`，把 `a` 存入這個 list。這就是 adjacency list：每個節點擁有一份清單，記錄它所有 outgoing edges 的目的地。

同時建立 `remaining[a]`，初值是進入 `a` 的 prerequisite edges 數量。這個 incoming-edge count 常稱為 indegree。完成一些課程後，我們使用的意義則是：`a` 還有幾門 prerequisite 尚未完成。計數為二，代表還有兩項不同的義務；只記錄課程是否有 prerequisite，會失去第一次完成先修課後所需的資訊。

使用 `after = [[] for _ in range(numCourses)]`。每門課分別求值一次 `[]`，就會得到各自獨立的 inner lists。若寫成 `[[]] * numCourses`，則會重複保存指向同一個 shared list 的 references：為課程 0 加上一門 dependent，其他課程也會看似同時多出那門 dependent。相較之下，這裡的 `[0] * numCourses` 是安全的。integer 是 immutable，而 `remaining[a] += 1` 會替換 slot `a` 裡的值，不會修改一個共用的零。Python 的 [sequence operations](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/stdtypes.html#common-sequence-operations) 區分重複 references 與複製它們指向的 objects。

把可開始的課程放入 `ready`，一個 queue。queue 保存等待處理的 entries；從一端移除最早進入的 entry，再從另一端加入新 entries，就得到 first-in, first-out 行為。在可開始的課程之間任選一門，不會破壞先修要求：每門被選的課都已經沒有未完成的 prerequisite。FIFO 讓 trace 有明確順序，也不必搜尋最小的課程編號。

使用沒有長度上限的 `collections.deque`。`deque()` 建立 queue，`append(x)` 把 `x` 加在右端並回傳 `None`，`popleft()` 則移除並回傳最左端的 entry。因此，若把 `append` 的回傳值重新指定給 `ready`，queue 就會被換成 `None`。有長度上限的 deque 在滿載時可能丟棄 entries，所以這裡不該設定 `maxlen`。這些行為由 [Python 3.14 deque documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/collections.html#collections.deque) 規定。

每當一門課從 `ready` 被移除，就在 `finished` 多記一次完成。只走訪 `after[course]` 裡的 dependents。每門 dependent 都恰好少了一項未滿足的義務，所以把其計數減一。恰好在某門 dependent 的計數變成零時，將它 append 進 queue。這個階段的計數只減不增。原本為正的計數只會跨越零一次，初始計數為零的課程則在初始化時入列，因此每門課最多進入 queue 一次，不需要額外的 visited set。

## 一段包含延後釋放的 program movie

考慮以下構造的輸入：

```text
numCourses = 5
prerequisites = [[1, 0], [2, 0], [3, 1], [3, 2]]
```

課程 4 獨立存在。課程 0 會釋放 1 與 2；兩者都完成後，3 才能開始。依照 pairs 列出的順序讀入，得到：

```text
after     = [[1, 2], [3], [3], [], []]
remaining = [0, 1, 1, 2, 0]
ready     = deque([0, 4])
finished  = 0
```

初始化依課程識別碼由小到大檢查，因此 0 比 4 先入列。此時 `popleft()` 回傳 0，並把 `ready` 修改成 `[4]`。增加 `finished` 後，得到 1。第一門 dependent 是 1：其計數從 1 變成 0，因此 `append(1)` 讓 queue 變成 `[4, 1]`。第二門 dependent 是 2：其計數也從 1 變成 0，得到 `[4, 1, 2]`。此時計數為 `[0, 0, 0, 2, 0]`。

下一次移除回傳 4，留下 `[1, 2]`；`finished` 變成 2。它的 dependent list 是空的，所以沒有計數改變。一門 isolated course 即使沒有釋放其他課，也算完成一門課。

移除 1 後留下 `[2]`，`finished` 增為 3。課程 3 的計數從 2 變成 1。零值檢查不成立：3 仍不能進入 queue，因為課程 2 尚未完成。若只用 Boolean 表示 readiness，就容易錯誤處理這個 branch。

移除 2 後 queue 清空，`finished` 增為 4。課程 3 的計數從 1 變成 0。加入 3 後得到 `[3]`，計數為 `[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]`。最後移除 3，queue 清空且 `finished = 5`；它的 dependent list 是空的。loop 結束，`5 == numCourses` 回傳 `True`。概念上的完成順序是 `[0, 4, 1, 2, 3]`；回傳 Boolean 的實作不會保存這個順序。

再看一個拒絕案例：`numCourses = 3`，pairs 是 `[[1, 0], [0, 1]]`。初始計數為 `[1, 1, 0]`，只有課程 2 進入 queue。它完成後沒有釋放其他課。此時 queue 為空，但 `finished = 1`，因此與 3 比較後回傳 `False`。有一門可開始的課並不足夠：另一個 component 仍包含 cycle。

## 完整 Python 解法與它的 checkpoint

```python
from collections import deque


class Solution:
    def canFinish(self, numCourses: int, prerequisites: list[list[int]]) -> bool:
        after = [[] for _ in range(numCourses)]
        remaining = [0] * numCourses

        for course, prerequisite in prerequisites:
            after[prerequisite].append(course)
            remaining[course] += 1

        ready = deque()
        for course in range(numCourses):
            if remaining[course] == 0:
                ready.append(course)

        finished = 0
        while ready:
            course = ready.popleft()
            finished += 1
            for dependent in after[course]:
                remaining[dependent] -= 1
                if remaining[dependent] == 0:
                    ready.append(dependent)

        return finished == numCourses
```

checkpoint 位於每次求值 `while ready` 之前，也就是前一門課完成後的所有更新都已處理完畢之時。此時，`finished` 計算互不相同的已完成課程；每門未完成課程的計數，等於它尚未完成的 prerequisites 數量；queue 恰好包含所有可以開始、尚未完成的課程，而且每門只出現一次。已完成的課程不在 queue 中。queue 內部的排列順序是實作選擇，與這些條件分開。

起初沒有課程完成，因此從所有 pairs 建立的計數具有所需意義。初始化掃描恰好納入計數為零的課程。因此，在第一次 iteration 之前 checkpoint 成立，即使 queue 起初就是空的也一樣。

對 maintenance 而言，移除一門可開始的課是合法的，因為它的 prerequisites 已全部完成。它的 outgoing edges 恰好描述這次完成所滿足的義務。把那些目的地的計數減一，會正確更新計數，而不影響其他課程。每個新降到零的目的地入列一次；其他已可開始的課程繼續留在 queue。增加 `finished` 便記錄了這一次新完成。checkpoint 會在整份 dependent list 處理結束後再次成立，而不是處理到一半時就成立。

對 termination 而言，最多只能移除 `numCourses` 門互不相同的課程。如果全部都被移除，這些合法步驟便構成 schedule。否則，queue 已空，但仍有課未完成。依 checkpoint，每門這樣的課都還有一門未完成的 prerequisite。前面的有限集合往回追蹤論證因此會找到 cycle，所以不可能存在完整 schedule。最後的比較因而涵蓋兩種結果。這個 algorithm 常稱為 Kahn's topological sort；topological order 會把每門 prerequisite 排在其 dependent 前面。

一個誘人的錯誤回傳方式，是只要初始 queue 非空就回傳 `True`。前面的三門課拒絕案例就能推翻它。如果要求案例必須同時含有 two-course cycle 與另一門可開始的課，則它按課程數計算是最小的：兩個課程識別碼形成 cycle，第三個提供誤導性的起點。如果沒有這項要求，更小的 `numCourses = 2, prerequisites = [[0, 0]]` 已能推翻捷徑：課程 1 可開始，但課程 0 在等待自己。

## Running time 從何而來

令 `V = numCourses`、`E = len(prerequisites)`。Big O 描述成長速度的 upper bound，忽略固定倍數；在下面的模型中，`O(V + E)` 表示工作量的成長不超過課程數加 pairs 數再乘上一個常數。讀取或寫入一個 list slot、比較有界的 integers、增加 counter，以及搬移或保存一個 object reference，都是固定大小的 elementary operations。課程識別碼介於 0 到 1999，計數介於 0 到 5000；在這個 contract 下，把這些 scalars 當成有界的單位是適當的。這是 operation-count model，不是說每個 Python instruction 的實際執行時間完全一樣。配置或複製 `k` 個 slots 的成本與 `k` 成正比。

queue 的選擇會影響這項計算。Python list 把 references 放在連續、有索引的 slots 裡。移除第一項後，必須把後面的 references 向左移，才能讓 indexing 繼續從零開始。如果初始有 `V` 門可開始的課，用 `pop(0)` 逐一取空 list，總共會搬移 `(V - 1) + (V - 2) + ... + 1` 個 references。將各項配對可得 `V(V - 1)/2`；即使完全沒有 prerequisite edges，仍是 quadratic growth。[Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.14/tutorial/datastructures.html#using-lists-as-queues) 說明了這種搬移成本。

CPython v3.14.0 的 [deque implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Modules/_collectionsmodule.c) 使用以 links 串接的固定長度 blocks。endpoint operation 會改變端點位置；遇到 block boundary 時，會改變固定大小 block 的連接，而不會把所有已入列的 references 搬移。如果把固定大小的 block allocation 視為有界工作，那麼在此模型中，每次 queue endpoint operation 都有 constant cost，與文件所述約為 `O(1)` 的行為相符。queue 大小可以增加，但單次 endpoint update 的工作量不會隨其長度增加。

adjacency lists 使用 `list.append`，需要另一個論證。list 有時會用完已配置的 slots。CPython v3.14.0 的 [list resize policy](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Objects/listobject.c) 在單項增加時預留 spare capacity；預留部分約為所要求大小的八分之一，另有少量 rounding 與 padding。一次成長可能複製原有 references，所以單次 append 並不保證都是 constant work。

# Course Schedule: count the obligations that remain

Suppose course 3 requires both course 1 and course 2. Finishing course 1 helps, but course 3 is still unavailable. A solution must remember how many requirements remain, then notice the moment that number becomes zero.

## What finishing all courses means

In [LeetCode 207](https://leetcode.com/problems/course-schedule/), course identifiers run from `0` through `numCourses - 1`. A pair `[a, b]` means that `b` must be finished before `a`. Return a Boolean indicating whether every course can be finished. A schedule itself is not required. There are 1 to 2000 courses and 0 to 5000 distinct prerequisite pairs; both identifiers belong to the course range. The statement does not exclude `[a, a]`, which makes that course impossible to start. The implementation below leaves the input unchanged.

A course with no requirements may be taken immediately. A course absent from every pair still exists and must count toward the result. Conversely, `[[1, 0], [0, 1]]` makes courses 0 and 1 wait for each other. No choice of first course can satisfy those requirements.

Draw a directed edge `b -> a` for `[a, b]`. A directed graph is simply the collection of course nodes and these one-way prerequisite edges. A directed cycle follows one or more edges back to its starting node. Each course on that cycle must wait for another course on the same cycle, so there can be no first completion there. A self-loop is a cycle containing one node.

The converse also holds for this finite graph. If every remaining course has a remaining prerequisite, start at any remaining course and repeatedly follow a prerequisite backward. There are finitely many course identifiers. Some identifier must repeat, which exposes a cycle. Thus a nonempty remainder without a cycle must contain an available course. Repeatedly taking an available course can finish everything exactly when the graph has no directed cycle. This equivalence describes the task; a changing loop invariant will describe our implementation.

## Retain a count and the courses it can release

Scanning every pair after every completion would rediscover which courses depend on the completed one. Instead, build `after[b]`, a list of courses directly waiting for `b`. Store `a` in that list for each pair `[a, b]`. This is an adjacency list: each node owns the list of destinations of its outgoing edges.

Also build `remaining[a]`, initially the number of incoming prerequisite edges for `a`. This incoming-edge count is often called indegree. After some completions, its useful meaning changes to the number of prerequisites of `a` that have not yet been completed. A count of two means that two distinct obligations remain; knowing only whether the course has any prerequisites would lose the information needed after the first completion.

Use `after = [[] for _ in range(numCourses)]`. Evaluating `[]` separately for each course makes independent inner lists. Writing `[[]] * numCourses` would repeat references to one shared list: adding a dependent for course 0 would also appear to add it for every other course. In contrast, `[0] * numCourses` is safe here. Integers are immutable, and `remaining[a] += 1` replaces the value in slot `a`; it does not mutate a shared zero. Python's [sequence operations](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/stdtypes.html#common-sequence-operations) distinguish repetition of references from copying their objects.

Keep available courses in `ready`, a queue. The queue holds entries waiting to be processed; removing the oldest entry and adding new entries at the other end gives first-in, first-out behavior. The choice among available courses cannot invalidate a requirement: each chosen course already has no unfinished prerequisite. FIFO supplies a definite trace without searching for the smallest course number.

Use an unbounded `collections.deque`. `deque()` creates the queue, `append(x)` adds `x` on the right and returns `None`, and `popleft()` removes and returns the leftmost entry. Assigning the result of `append` back to `ready` would therefore replace the queue with `None`. A bounded deque can discard entries when full, so no `maxlen` belongs here. These behaviors are specified by the [Python 3.14 deque documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/collections.html#collections.deque).

Whenever a course is removed from `ready`, mark one more completion in `finished`. Visit only its dependents in `after[course]`. Each loses exactly one outstanding obligation, so subtract one from its count. Append a dependent precisely when its count becomes zero. Counts never increase during this phase. A positive count crosses zero only once, and initially zero courses enter during initialization, so each course enters the queue at most once. No additional visited set is needed.

## A program movie with a delayed release

Consider this constructed input:

```text
numCourses = 5
prerequisites = [[1, 0], [2, 0], [3, 1], [3, 2]]
```

Course 4 is independent. Course 0 releases 1 and 2; both must finish before 3. Reading the pairs in their listed order produces:

```text
after     = [[1, 2], [3], [3], [], []]
remaining = [0, 1, 1, 2, 0]
ready     = deque([0, 4])
finished  = 0
```

Initialization checks course identifiers in increasing order, so 0 enters before 4. Now `popleft()` returns 0 and mutates `ready` to `[4]`. Incrementing `finished` gives 1. The first dependent is 1: its count changes from 1 to 0, so `append(1)` makes the queue `[4, 1]`. The second dependent is 2: its count also changes from 1 to 0, producing `[4, 1, 2]`. Counts are now `[0, 0, 0, 2, 0]`.

The next removal returns 4, leaving `[1, 2]`; `finished` becomes 2. Its dependent list is empty, so no count changes. An isolated course contributes a completion even though it releases nothing.

Removing 1 leaves `[2]` and raises `finished` to 3. Course 3 changes from 2 to 1. The zero test fails: 3 stays out of the queue because course 2 is still unfinished. This is the branch a Boolean notion of readiness would mishandle.

Removing 2 empties the queue and raises `finished` to 4. Course 3 changes from 1 to 0. Appending 3 gives `[3]`, with counts `[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]`. Finally, removing 3 gives an empty queue and `finished = 5`; its dependent list is empty. The loop stops and `5 == numCourses` returns `True`. The conceptual completion sequence is `[0, 4, 1, 2, 3]`; the Boolean implementation does not retain it.

For a rejection, use `numCourses = 3` and `[[1, 0], [0, 1]]`. Initial counts are `[1, 1, 0]`, and only course 2 enters the queue. It finishes without releasing anything. The empty queue now accompanies `finished = 1`, so the comparison with 3 returns `False`. Having one available course was insufficient: a different component still contains a cycle.

## Complete Python solution and its checkpoint

```python
from collections import deque


class Solution:
    def canFinish(self, numCourses: int, prerequisites: list[list[int]]) -> bool:
        after = [[] for _ in range(numCourses)]
        remaining = [0] * numCourses

        for course, prerequisite in prerequisites:
            after[prerequisite].append(course)
            remaining[course] += 1

        ready = deque()
        for course in range(numCourses):
            if remaining[course] == 0:
                ready.append(course)

        finished = 0
        while ready:
            course = ready.popleft()
            finished += 1
            for dependent in after[course]:
                remaining[dependent] -= 1
                if remaining[dependent] == 0:
                    ready.append(dependent)

        return finished == numCourses
```

The checkpoint is just before each evaluation of `while ready`, after all updates for the preceding completion. At that point, `finished` counts distinct completed courses; every unfinished course's count equals its number of unfinished prerequisites; and the queue contains every available unfinished course exactly once. Completed courses are outside the queue. The queue's internal order is an implementation choice, separate from these conditions.

Initially nothing is completed, so the counts built from all pairs have the required meaning. The initialization scan includes exactly the zero-count courses. Thus the checkpoint holds before the first iteration, including when the queue is initially empty.

For maintenance, removing an available course is legal because all its prerequisites are completed. Its outgoing edges describe exactly the obligations that this completion satisfies. Decrementing those destinations updates the counts correctly, without changing any unrelated count. Each destination newly reaching zero enters once; other available courses remain queued. Increasing `finished` records this one new completion. The checkpoint holds again after the whole dependent list is processed, rather than midway through it.

For termination, at most `numCourses` distinct courses can be removed. If all were removed, those legal steps establish a schedule. Otherwise the queue is empty with some courses unfinished. The checkpoint says each such course still has an unfinished prerequisite. The finite backward-following argument above then finds a cycle, so no full schedule is possible. The final comparison therefore covers both results. This algorithm is often called Kahn's topological sort; a topological order places every prerequisite before its dependent.

A tempting wrong return is `True` whenever the initial queue is nonempty. The three-course rejection above refutes it. It is smallest by number of courses if a two-course cycle and a separate available course are required: two course identifiers form the cycle and a third supplies the misleading start. Without that requirement, the smaller `numCourses = 2, prerequisites = [[0, 0]]` already refutes the shortcut: course 1 is available while course 0 waits for itself.

## Where the running time comes from

Let `V = numCourses` and `E = len(prerequisites)`. Big O describes an upper bound on growth, ignoring fixed multipliers; `O(V + E)` means work grows no faster than a constant times the number of courses plus pairs, under the following model. Reading or writing one list slot, comparing bounded integers, incrementing a counter, and moving or retaining one object reference are elementary constant-size operations. Course identifiers fit within 0 to 1999 and counts within 0 to 5000; treating these scalars as bounded units is appropriate for this contract. This is an operation-count model, not a statement that all Python instructions take identical physical time. Allocating or copying `k` slots costs proportional to `k`.

The queue choice affects this count. A Python list stores references in consecutive indexed slots. Removing its first item must shift the later references left so indexing still starts at zero. With `V` initially available courses, draining a list through `pop(0)` moves `(V - 1) + (V - 2) + ... + 1` references. Pairing the terms gives `V(V - 1)/2`, quadratic growth even with no prerequisite edges. The [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.14/tutorial/datastructures.html#using-lists-as-queues) describes the shifting cost.

CPython v3.14.0's [deque implementation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Modules/_collectionsmodule.c) uses fixed-length blocks joined by links. An endpoint operation changes an endpoint position and, at a block boundary, a fixed-size block connection; it does not shift all queued references. With fixed-size block allocation treated as bounded work, each queue endpoint operation has constant cost in this model, matching the documented approximately `O(1)` behavior. Queue size can grow, but the work of a single endpoint update does not grow with it.

Adjacency lists use `list.append`, which needs a different argument. A list sometimes runs out of allocated slots. CPython v3.14.0's [list resize policy](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/v3.14.0/Objects/listobject.c) reserves spare capacity on single-item growth, roughly one eighth of the requested size beyond the items, with small rounding and padding. A growth may copy the old references, so one append is not always constant work.

Here is why a whole append-only sequence is still linear. After growing a sufficiently large list of size `m`, proportional spare room allows at least a fixed fraction of `m` further single-item appends before another growth. Charge the cost proportional to `m` of that growth across those following appends; each receives only a constant charge. Equivalently, look backward from final capacity `C`: successive earlier growth sizes shrink by a fixed factor below one, apart from small sizes. Their copying work is bounded by `C + rC + r²C + ... = C/(1-r)` for some fixed `r < 1`. To see the bound, multiplying the sum by `r` leaves the original sum minus its first term; subtraction gives `(1-r)S = C`. Small initial capacities add fixed work. Final capacity is proportional to the final length, so `d` single-item appends, including their ordinary writes, take `O(d)` total work. This aggregate guarantee is called amortized constant time per append. It applies here because each adjacency list only grows by one appended item at a time; no alternating deletion or bulk update is being smuggled into the argument.

Building the `V` independent lists and `V` counts costs `O(V)`. Reading `E` pairs does `E` counter updates and `E` appends. If course `b` has `d_b` dependents, its append sequence costs `O(d_b)`; summing `d_b` across all courses gives exactly `E`. Small-list overhead contributes at most another `O(V)`. Building the representation therefore costs `O(V + E)`.

The readiness scan checks `V` slots and enqueues at most `V` courses. During processing, each course is enqueued and removed at most once. Each edge appears in exactly one dependent list, and that list is visited at most once. Hence all executions of the inner loop total at most `E`, even though the code nests that loop inside a `while`. Setup, queue operations and edge updates sum to worst-case `O(V + E)` time, with list construction analyzed over its append sequences. A cycle may stop processing early, but cannot avoid the initial pair-reading work.

For auxiliary space, the outer adjacency list and its inner-list headers use `O(V)` slots or fixed-size records. The inner lists retain `E` references plus spare capacity proportional to `V + E`, by the same growth policy. Counts use `V` scalar slots, and the queue holds at most `V` entries plus fixed-size block overhead proportional to that capacity. Scalar loop variables need constant space. A resize can temporarily keep old and new storage alive, but both have size proportional to the list being grown; this leaves the peak bound `O(V + E)`. The existing input is excluded from auxiliary space, and the returned Boolean is `O(1)` output space. No recursion stack is used.

## Trading stored edges for repeated scans

If storing another `E` references is unacceptable but the original pair list can be scanned repeatedly, there is a slower alternative. Keep `done[V]` Booleans. In each round, allocate a fresh `blocked[V]` array of false values. Scan every pair `[a, b]`; if both `a` and `b` are unfinished, set `blocked[a]` to true. Then identify all unfinished, unblocked courses and mark that whole group done only after the scan has finished. These are exactly the courses with no unfinished prerequisite at the start of that round. Stop successfully when all are done, or unsuccessfully when a round adds none.

The same legality and finite-cycle argument applies to these groups. Group members cannot require one another, since any such edge would have marked its destination blocked. Each successful round completes at least one new course, so there are at most `V` successful rounds and at most one final failed round. Initializing flags and inspecting courses costs `O(V)` per round; checking every pair costs `O(E)`. The resulting bound is `O(V(V + E))`. A length-`V` prerequisite chain releases only one course per round, showing why the repeated work can persist as size grows. `done`, `blocked` and an optional group buffer each hold at most `V` entries, so peak auxiliary storage is `O(V)`; old round buffers are released before the next round. The Boolean output stays `O(1)`. The input's `E` pairs remain live and are excluded under the same convention. Prefer this trade-off only when the extra adjacency storage matters more than repeated scans.

A different requirement changes what the main solution must retain: return one valid course order, or `[]` if impossible. Start an empty `order` list and append `course` immediately after each removal. Return `order` if its length equals `V`, otherwise return `[]`. Each retained entry records a legal completion, so the earlier proof establishes the returned ordering. No smallest-first guarantee follows from FIFO; for the movie, 4 appears before 1.

This adaptation adds at most `V` single-item appends to one growing list. The append-only argument still applies, so the added work is `O(V)` and the whole algorithm remains `O(V + E)`. The adjacency representation, counts and queue remain, so auxiliary storage excluding a successful returned order stays `O(V + E)`. Successful output contains exactly `V` references and takes `O(V)` output space. On failure, the partial order is temporary auxiliary storage of at most `V` entries and the returned empty list has constant size. Keeping an order changes storage accounting, not the cost of visiting each edge.
